title: v1/chat: coordinator for stop-ranking, role resolution, and logprob abstraction
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: We continue to converge the Redwood API surface with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions expectations while preserving the runtime semantics and safety guarantees of the platform. Customers expect consistent handling of 'stop' semantics, role aliases, and token-level diagnostics (logprobs) across streaming and non-streaming paths. Motivation: Prior implementations duplicated stop heuristics across the streaming coordinator and the batched inference path, which led to subtle differences for edge cases (multi-token stops, weighted stop lists) and made tool/function-calling integration brittle during stream handoffs. This PR centralizes stop ranking and logprob post-processing into a small coordinator layer that sits between the compatibility layer and the runtime, and adds an explicit role-resolution pass to keep role aliasing deterministic.

What this PR does: 1) Introduces a lightweight ChatParamCoordinator that normalizes incoming /v1/chat parameters (stop arrays, stop-weights, role aliases, temperature/nucleus fallbacks) into a single canonical representation used by both streaming and batch paths. 2) Adds a StopRanking module that computes a prioritized stop prediction list using model token boundaries and span-level scoring; it produces a stable stop decision object consumed by the stream-framer and the final message serializer. 3) Extracts logprob abstraction helpers so tooling (SDKs and observability) can request per-token top-k scores without duplicating formatting logic. 4) Adds role resolution mapping (role_alias -> canonical_role) and ensures the mapping is recorded in the response metadata returned both in streaming deltas and the final framed JSON envelope. 5) Small SDK bindings and example demonstrating a predictable fncall handoff when a tool returns a stop-inducing token sequence.

Behavioral guarantees and compatibility: - Backwards compatible default behavior: if a request uses legacy fields, coordinator will map them to the canonical form. - Streaming parity: streamed deltas include a sentinel when a StopRanking decision is reached; clients using framed json will receive identical final message shapes as non-streaming completions. - Logprobs: the abstraction returns scores in OpenAI-compatible arrays (token, logprob, top_logprobs) but the internal representation remains optimized for vectorized retrieval. - Safety: StopRanking enforces a minimum safety filter pass (configured via runtime flag) so that stop tokens flagged by the safety subsystem are treated with priority.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for coordinator normalization and stop-ranking heuristics (tests/unit/chat/coordinator_test.rs). - Integration tests exercising streaming/non-streaming parity across role aliasing and multi-stop lists (tests/integration/chatv1_stop_compat.test). - Added e2e scenario in examples/compatibility/chat_tooling_example.py demonstrating function-call -> tool -> resume flow when tool output contains stop tokens. - Benchmarked tail-latency impact: coordinator adds ~0.3ms median and <1.5ms p95 on a 512-token window in our canary environment; included micro-optimizations to keep path hot.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind `chatv1_param_coordinator` flag; gradual canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then full. If regressions observed, flag can be toggled to restore previous per-path heuristics.

Checklist: - [x] Coordinator implementation and unit tests - [x] Stream-framer integration and delta sentinel - [x] SDK example updated - [x] Observability added (trace/span for stop decisions) - [x] Performance microbench and notes included

Notes: This is intentionally non-breaking; however, customers that relied on previous stop tie-breaking may observe deterministic but different choices in certain multi-stop/overlapping token cases. We will surface this in release notes and the console rollout modal.

review_comments: Mateo Ruiz (Reviewer): Can we avoid copying token arrays twice in the framer? Suggest passing a token view and annotating boundaries instead of cloning. Requested change noted.
Aisha Patel (Author): Switched to token views and annotated in-place; updated framer to hold a small lifetime-bound reference in coordinator path.
Lin Qiao (Reviewer): Add a short note in docs explaining deterministic tie-breaking for overlapping stops so users can anticipate behavior. Approved after docs update.
Jamal Thompson (SRE): Verified canary logs for stop-decision spans and trace spans look sane; minor suggestion to reduce p95 noise in metrics aggregation; resolved.
release_notes: Add ChatParamCoordinator to normalize /v1/chat parameters and produce stable stop decisions across streaming and batch paths. Role alias resolution and OpenAI-compatible logprob formatting are now unified. Backwards-compatible by default; customers may see different deterministic tie-breaking in overlapping 'stop' cases.
